short_answer: Indian Cowboy is the selling name of Arun Shiva, a handicapper on the Doc's Sports roster. On 17 Nov 2026 his Doc's profile listed football, college basketball, NBA, NHL and soccer packages for the 2026 to 2027 seasons, and a Doc's page carried a 6 unit college basketball play from him for Monday 16 Nov 2026. In that narrow sense he is a real, current seller.

Whether his picks make money over time is a separate question. Doc's credits him with 84 wins and 54 losses, +10,300, in college basketball last season and several winning NBA years, but every number comes from the company that sells him. We found no full, time stamped log of every pick kept by anyone else.

Independent buyer talk is thin. The one buyer story we found, from 2024, is negative and secondhand. Treat him as an unproven seller, read the guarantee wording before paying, and record every pick yourself with the line and time you got it.

guarantee: On football packages his profile says the weekly package is "backed by our profit guarantee," and the monthly one adds that "you can use our self-extend service if we do not produce a profit." The NBA weekly package says the same: "If your package finishes at a loss, you can extend your service for free through our self-extend program."

On day packages the remedy is account credit. The NHL day package says that if it "results in a loss (or profit less than $35) you will have a $30 credit put back into your account," and the college basketball day package mentions a $30 account credit the following morning.

We found no cash refund terms on the Doc's pages we opened. A buyer who loses gets more picks or store credit. Losses on the bets themselves are never covered, and they are usually far larger than the package price.

claims_note: Some figures disagree between sections of the same profile. The soccer season appears as +16,170, +16,600 and +17,200 in different places.
The NBA lines do not add up cleanly either: "3 straight winning seasons +10,000" sits next to "+4500" for 2025 and "2500" for 2024, which leaves the third season unexplained.
A count of 7 and 0 weeks is a highlight reel. Anyone who bets one play a day for years will have many perfect weeks and many losing ones; the page shows only the first kind.

A 2 Jan 2020 newsletter from a partner site credited him with close to +11,000 across NHL, NBA and college basketball in 2019 and pointed readers to a free trial at Doc's. That is promotion, not an audit.
record: What a buyer can verify independently: nothing that we could find. We found no full, time stamped log of every Indian Cowboy pick with the line, the odds and the release time, kept by anyone other than the seller, and no court or regulator record about him.

What the seller publishes: Doc's Sports pages show season totals, streaks and a table of the previous day's results by handicapper. On the college basketball page we read on 17 Nov 2026, his line in the most recent results table showed minus 6 units, or minus $660 on Doc's scale, so the table does include losing days. Doc's grades these on its own numbers.
The Doc's NHL page says he went 61%, +8,700 in one of two winning NHL seasons in 2020 and 2021. We could not check any of it.

our_data.text: Watchdog grades picks captured from public posts before the game starts. In this edition no Indian Cowboy pick history is matched to a Watchdog graded record, so we make no claim about how Indian Cowboy performs.
our_data.context: For scale: the season figures Doc's quotes for him sit around 61% winners. On the Watchdog board, {{over60}} of {{established}} established accounts (100 or more graded picks) were at 60% or better, and the median established account won {{median_win}}% of its picks. At standard -110 odds a bettor needs about 52.4% to break even.

customers_intro: Independent customer evidence on Indian Cowboy is thin. Below is everything we found and how much weight it can carry.

customers.text: We found one buyer story about Indian Cowboy outside the sites that sell or promote him: a 2024 Reddit post in which a bettor said a friend paid for a week of his picks, lost money, and was pitched a big parlay as a sure thing. The replies mostly mocked paying for picks in general rather than adding their own experience with him. Everything positive we found comes from Doc's Sports or a partner newsletter that sent readers to a Doc's trial. We found no reader reviews, no tracked buyer results and no complaints about billing. Our Reddit search was partial: the saved archive was searched in full, but fresh searches of several betting forums timed out. One negative secondhand post is not a pattern.

In r/sportsbook, a user warned others away from Indian Cowboy, saying a friend paid $395 for a week of picks and lost money despite a guarantee, and that a seven leg parlay was pitched as a lock. This is secondhand and unverified. The $395 figure does not match the $99 weekly packages on his Doc's profile today, so the friend may have bought a different product.

The 16 replies to that post were mostly jokes and general warnings against paying anyone for picks or trusting the word lock. One reply asked how he was still in business. None described buying his picks firsthand.

Doc's Sports pages describe big seasons in college basketball, the NBA, the NHL and soccer, a doctorate in biostatistics and a large YouTube audience. Doc's sells his packages, so this is marketing, not independent evidence.

The Rocketman Sports newsletter called him one of the most successful basketball bettors in the industry, quoted 2019 profits of close to +11,000, and offered a free trial from "our friends at Doc's Sports." It is promotion tied to the seller, not a buyer review.
TheRX daily service play thread lists "Doc's Sports" among services members may not post. The thread gives no reason, so it is a forum rule, not a judgment on Indian Cowboy.
We found no Sportsbook Review or Covers thread about him in web searches, and a December 2025 TheRX thread asking about Doc's Sports does not mention him.

conflicts: Every record and season total is published by Doc's Sports, which sells his packages.
The Doc's FAQ says "We have a list of offshore sports book that we have complete confidence in." Offshore sportsbooks are not licensed by U.S. state regulators.
The 2020 newsletter that praised him linked readers to a Doc's Sports trial, so it is not independent.
strengths: Prices and guarantee wording are published for every package.
Doc's shows the previous day's results, including his losing days, such as a minus 6 unit day in the table we read.
He posts free picks and videos, so a buyer can watch his reasoning before paying.
concerns: No full public record. Every number we saw comes from the seller.
Figures for the same season differ between sections of his profile.
The guarantee returns credit or free time, never cash.
The only buyer story we found is negative, though secondhand and unverified.
Doc's FAQ points readers to offshore sportsbooks.
checklist: Ask for every pick from the last 12 months with the line, the odds and the time it was sent. A season total on a sales page is not a record.
Count units, not wins. His plays are often 6 to 8 units, so one loss can wipe out several small wins.
Read the guarantee for the words refund, credit and extension. Here it is credit or free time.
Write down each pick yourself the moment you receive it, with the line you can actually get.
Start with a one day package before any season pass.
faq: He is a real, active handicapper named Arun Shiva whose picks are sold on Doc's Sports at published prices. We could not verify that his picks win over time, because the only records come from the seller, and we found no court or regulator action involving him.
How much does Indian Cowboy cost?
On 17 Nov 2026 his Doc's Sports profile sold one day packages for $30.00, weekly packages for $89.00 to $99.00, monthly packages from $279.00 to $325.00 and season packages from $495.00 to $850.00.
Does Indian Cowboy have a verified record?
No. Doc's quotes season totals such as 84 and 54 in college basketball and runs of perfect weeks, all published by the seller. We found no independent, time stamped log of every pick.

You get his daily plays with write ups, and on most packages a credit or free extension if the period loses. What is unproven is whether his picks beat the roughly 52.4% needed at -110 over hundreds of plays, and nothing refunds your betting losses.
